Industrias CH SAB de CV Reports Steady Steel Trade Volumes Amidst Moderate Demand

Industrias CH SAB de CV, one of Mexico’s prominent steel producers, reported routine trade figures for the latest quarter, demonstrating stable performance in line with broader industry trends. The company’s export and domestic sales volumes remained largely consistent with the previous quarter, according to data released Tuesday.

Total steel shipments for the period reached approximately 745,000 metric tons, reflecting a marginal year-over-year increase of 1.2%. Domestic demand for long and flat steel products continued to be supported by ongoing infrastructure projects and steady activity in Mexico’s manufacturing sector. Export volumes accounted for 38% of total shipments, with the United States and Central America remaining key destinations.

“We are encouraged by the sustained demand in both domestic and export markets,” said Juan Carlos Martínez, Chief Financial Officer at Industrias CH SAB de CV. “Our operational efficiency and supply chain stability have enabled us to meet client commitments without interruption.”

Industry observers noted that global steel prices have remained relatively stable in recent months, with cautious optimism prevailing among producers. “The Mexican steel sector is benefiting from gradual economic recovery and consistent construction activity,” said Ana López, an analyst at the National Chamber of the Iron and Steel Industry. “While there are no extraordinary developments this quarter, steady trade volumes are a positive sign for the sector’s resilience.”

The company’s routine trade figures were in line with expectations, according to union representatives. “There have been no disruptions affecting production or exports,” commented Julio Ramírez, spokesman for the Steelworkers Union. “The workforce remains engaged, and plant operations are running smoothly.”

Looking ahead, Industrias CH SAB de CV indicated that it expects similar trading conditions in the coming months, citing robust order books and continued infrastructure investment. Company officials refrained from issuing formal forecasts but reiterated their commitment to operational consistency and customer satisfaction. 

Shares of Industrias CH SAB de CV closed up 0.6% on the Mexican Stock Exchange following the release of the trade figures.
